verdict.rationale: The Gmail API uses OAuth 2.0 with granular scopes, and Google's docs tell developers to request the narrowest scope possible, including non-sensitive and read-only ones, so an agent's credential can be limited to specific features. However, scoping stops at the feature level: a community user notes that apps cannot be restricted to a specific label or folder. Nothing in the evidence describes agent-specific credential issuance or management. Missing for 10: per-label or per-mailbox-subset scoping, documented agent-oriented credential issuance, revocation and expiry controls, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Whenever possible, use non-sensitive scopes to narrow access to only the specific features needed by an app.
The Gmail IMAP, POP, and SMTP servers support authorization with the industry-standard OAuth 2.0 protocol.
Read-only mail extraction, indexing, and backup
Gmail API auth scopes already allow read-only access, but one user wants to restrict apps to a specific label or subfolder for better security without forwarding mail.
